blocks.text: iOS 5 reorganized daily interaction around Notification Center, iMessage, Newsstand, Reminders, system-level Twitter support, richer Camera and Photos tools, and broader Mail, Calendar, Game Center, keyboard, and accessibility features.

citations.locator: Notification Center, iMessage, Newsstand, Reminders, Twitter, Camera, Photos, Mail, Game Center, AirPlay, and split keyboard

blocks.text: The release also moved setup, software updating, and iTunes synchronization away from a required cable, integrated iCloud services, exposed more than 1,500 developer APIs, and delivered security work spanning credentials, certificate trust, TLS, documents, networking, Safari, and WebKit.

citations.locator: iOS 5 — PC Free, iCloud support, wireless sync, and developer APIs
More than 1,500 APIs and principal SDK technologies
iOS 5 and iCloud availability on October 12

blocks.text: iOS 5.0.1 addressed battery-life defects, brought multitasking gestures to the original iPad, repaired Documents in the Cloud behavior, and improved Australian English dictation recognition.
Its security bulletin also records fixes for URL and DNS handling, malicious fonts, certificate trust, code-signing enforcement, and an iPad 2 Smart Cover passcode-bypass condition.

iOS 5.1 added Japanese Siri support, Photo Stream deletion, more direct lock-screen Camera access, broader face highlighting, a redesigned iPad Camera app, new iTunes Match and iPad media controls, and targeted battery and call-audio repairs.

Apple’s security bulletin documents additional protections for network requests, disk images, the application sandbox, DNS parsing, passcode lock, Safari Private Browsing, Siri on the lock screen, VPN configuration files, and WebKit.

iOS 5.1.1 improved lock-screen HDR reliability, repaired cellular switching on the third-generation iPad, corrected AirPlay video playback, strengthened Safari bookmark and Reading List synchronization, and removed a misleading purchase alert.
The accompanying advisory describes a Safari location-bar spoofing fix and WebKit corrections for cross-site scripting and memory corruption.

events.summary: The public iOS 5 release introduced a broad communications, notification, cloud, media, productivity, device-independence, accessibility, developer-platform, and security update.

changes.title: Notification Center
changes.canonicalSummary: Notification Center consolidated alerts and added noninterruptive banners plus lock-screen access.
changes.summary: A downward swipe opened a unified notification view, incoming alerts could appear briefly at the top of the screen, and lock-screen items could lead directly to their associated app.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: iMessage
changes.canonicalSummary: iMessage added encrypted text, photo, and video conversations between devices running iOS 5.
changes.summary: The Messages app gained Wi-Fi and cellular conversations among iOS 5 devices, with group messaging, delivery and read receipts, and synchronization across a user’s devices.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Newsstand
changes.canonicalSummary: Newsstand organized periodical subscriptions and supported automatic background delivery of new issues.
changes.summary: Magazine and newspaper subscriptions received a dedicated Home Screen location that displayed current covers and could download newly available issues in the background.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Reminders
changes.canonicalSummary: A new Reminders app managed tasks with synchronization and supported time- or location-based alerts.
changes.summary: Users could organize tasks, synchronize them with iCloud, iCal, or Outlook, and on supported iPhones trigger reminders when arriving at or leaving a location.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: System Twitter integration
changes.canonicalSummary: A single system sign-in enabled direct posting from Apple apps and supplied integration APIs to developers.
changes.summary: Twitter credentials could be configured once in Settings and used from Camera, Photos, Maps, Safari, YouTube, and compatible third-party applications.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Faster and more controllable Camera
changes.canonicalSummary: Camera gained lock-screen access, volume-button capture, composition aids, zoom, and focus or exposure locking.
changes.summary: Supported devices could open Camera from the lock screen, use Volume Up as a shutter, enable grid lines, pinch to zoom, move between preview and Camera Roll, and lock focus or exposure where supported.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: On-device Photos editing
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos added cropping, rotation, red-eye removal, one-tap enhancement, and album organization.
changes.summary: The built-in Photos app could perform common corrections and organize images into albums without requiring a separate desktop workflow.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Expanded Mail composition and triage
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail added rich-text formatting, indentation, draggable recipients, flags, bulk state changes, custom sounds, and S/MIME.
changes.summary: Users gained more control over message formatting and addressing, could flag or mark multiple messages together, choose mail alert sounds, and use S/MIME.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Calendar views and attachments
changes.canonicalSummary: Calendar added new device-specific views, faster event creation, and event-attachment access.
changes.summary: The iPad received a year view, iPhone and iPod touch received a week view, tapping could create an event, and users could view or add event attachments.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Game Center profiles and discovery
changes.canonicalSummary: Game Center expanded profiles, score comparisons, friend discovery, and game recommendations.
changes.summary: Players could add profile photos, compare aggregate achievement scores, discover friends through recommendations and mutual connections, and receive customized game suggestions.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: AirPlay Mirroring and iPad multitasking gestures
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported iPads gained screen mirroring and four- or five-finger navigation gestures.
changes.summary: iPad 2 and iPhone 4S could mirror through Apple TV, while iPad 2 added gestures to return Home, reveal multitasking, or switch among applications.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5 — AirPlay Mirroring and Multitasking Gestures

changes.title: PC-free setup, over-the-air updates, and Wi-Fi Sync
changes.canonicalSummary: Devices could be activated and maintained without tethering and could synchronize with iTunes over Wi-Fi.
changes.summary: Setup Assistant enabled on-device activation and configuration, software updates could arrive over the air, and purchased content could synchronize wirelessly with an iTunes library.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5 — Setup Assistant, software updates, and wireless sync

changes.title: iCloud integration
changes.canonicalSummary: iCloud connected purchases, photos, documents, backup, communications data, and device location across supported products.
changes.summary: The operating system integrated iTunes in the Cloud, Photo Stream, Documents in the Cloud, purchase history and automatic downloads, backup, Contacts, Calendar, Mail, and Find My iPhone.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Keyboard and input improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Keyboard updates added an iPad split layout, better correction and East Asian input, Emoji, a personal dictionary, and text shortcuts.
changes.summary: The release expanded keyboard layouts and language behavior while allowing users to define shortcuts for frequently typed words or phrases.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Broader accessibility controls
changes.canonicalSummary: Accessibility additions covered visual alerts, custom vibration, assistive input, spoken selections, and VoiceOver labeling.
changes.summary: Supported iPhones could flash the LED or use custom vibration patterns for alerts, and the system added mobility-device input, Speak Selection, and custom element labels for VoiceOver.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Exchange ActiveSync workflow improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Exchange accounts gained task synchronization, message-state controls, offline improvements, and GAL contact saving.
changes.summary: Users could synchronize tasks wirelessly, flag or mark messages, work more effectively offline, and save new contacts from a Global Address List.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: More than 1,500 new developer APIs
changes.canonicalSummary: The iOS 5 SDK exposed more than 1,500 APIs supporting the release’s new platform capabilities.
changes.summary: Apple described an SDK expansion spanning iCloud storage, Notification Center, Newsstand, iMessage, Twitter integration, Game Center, and other platform technologies.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5 — More than 1,500 new developer APIs
iOS 5 SDK and more than 1,500 new APIs

changes.title: Credential, certificate, and TLS hardening
changes.canonicalSummary: Security changes protected stored credentials, removed or constrained unsafe certificate trust, and added TLS 1.2.
changes.summary: Apple stopped locally logging Apple ID and Wi-Fi credentials, distrusted DigiNotar certificates, restricted MD5-signed certificates, and added TLS 1.2 support.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: CFNetwork credential logging; Data Security certificate trust and TLS; Wi-Fi credential logging

changes.title: Content parsing and web-origin security
changes.canonicalSummary: The release corrected representative memory-safety, document-isolation, URL-spoofing, and cross-origin defects.
changes.summary: Apple documented repairs across CoreFoundation, CoreGraphics, ImageIO, ICU, libxml, OfficeImport, Safari, and WebKit, including code-execution and cross-origin risks.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: CoreFoundation, CoreGraphics, ImageIO, ICU, libxml, OfficeImport, Safari, and WebKit

events.summary: The public iOS 5.0.1 update combined four documented consumer improvements with targeted network, font, certificate, kernel, and lock-screen security repairs.

changes.title: Battery-life repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: The update corrected unspecified defects that affected battery life.
changes.summary: Apple’s consumer note identifies battery-life bug fixes without attributing a single battery symptom or device-specific cause.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Multitasking gestures for the original iPad
changes.canonicalSummary: The original iPad gained the multitasking gestures introduced for iPad 2 in iOS 5.
changes.summary: iOS 5.0.1 extended the documented multitasking gesture feature to the first-generation iPad.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Documents in the Cloud repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: The update resolved unspecified defects affecting Documents in the Cloud.
changes.summary: Apple records a Documents in the Cloud repair but does not itemize the affected applications or failure modes.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Australian dictation recognition
changes.canonicalSummary: Voice recognition improved for Australian users who used dictation.
changes.summary: The dictation system received a language-region-specific recognition improvement for Australian users.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: URL and DNS routing validation
changes.canonicalSummary: CFNetwork and libinfo were corrected to avoid routing crafted URLs or hostnames to unintended servers.
changes.summary: Apple fixed URL and DNS lookup defects that could disclose sensitive information by resolving or navigating to an incorrect server.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: FreeType font-processing hardening
changes.canonicalSummary: CoreGraphics corrected FreeType memory-corruption defects reachable through crafted fonts.
changes.summary: The update addressed multiple font-processing memory-corruption issues, including cases Apple said could enable arbitrary code execution.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: DigiCert Malaysia trust restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: Default trust settings stopped trusting DigiCert Malaysia certificates associated with weak intermediates.
changes.summary: Apple changed certificate trust after weak intermediate certificates could not be revoked, reducing interception risk for affected certificate chains.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Code-signing enforcement
changes.canonicalSummary: The kernel corrected mmap flag validation that could allow unsigned code to execute.
changes.summary: A kernel logic error in validation of mmap flag combinations was repaired to prevent bypassing code-signing checks.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: iPad 2 Smart Cover passcode protection
changes.canonicalSummary: The update closed a locked-state Smart Cover sequence that exposed limited data without a passcode.
changes.summary: Apple corrected an iPad 2 condition in which opening a Smart Cover during power-off confirmation could bypass the normal passcode prompt and expose some data.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

events.summary: The public iOS 5.1 update expanded Siri, Camera, Photo Stream, media, and carrier presentation behavior while addressing battery, calling, lock-screen, networking, and web security defects.

changes.title: Japanese Siri support
changes.canonicalSummary: Siri added Japanese language support, subject to Apple’s initial availability qualification.
changes.summary: The voice assistant expanded to Japanese, with Apple warning that availability could be limited during the initial rollout.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5.1 — Japanese language support for Siri

changes.title: Photo Stream deletion
changes.canonicalSummary: Users could delete photos directly from Photo Stream.
changes.summary: Photo Stream gained an explicit deletion capability for removing individual images.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Camera access, face detection, and iPad redesign
changes.canonicalSummary: Camera became persistently accessible from supported lock screens, highlighted every detected face, and gained a redesigned iPad interface.
changes.summary: The lock-screen Camera shortcut was made continuously visible on listed devices, face detection highlighted all recognized faces, and the iPad Camera app received a new design.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Genius for iTunes Match
changes.canonicalSummary: iTunes Match subscribers gained Genius Mixes and Genius playlists.
changes.summary: The Music experience exposed Genius-created mixes and playlists to users with an iTunes Match subscription.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5.1 — Genius for iTunes Match subscribers

changes.title: iPad media audio and podcast controls
changes.canonicalSummary: iPad media playback gained clearer audio tuning plus podcast speed and rewind controls.
changes.summary: Apple optimized TV-show and movie audio for greater clarity and volume and added podcast playback-speed control with a 30-second rewind.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5.1 — iPad media and podcast controls

changes.title: AT&T network indicator
changes.canonicalSummary: The update changed the network indicator shown for AT&T service.
changes.summary: Apple records an updated AT&T network indicator without describing any underlying radio or throughput change.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Battery-life repairs
changes.canonicalSummary: The update corrected unspecified defects that affected battery life.
changes.summary: Apple lists battery-life bug fixes but does not assign them to a particular device, subsystem, or reproducible symptom.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Outgoing-call audio reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: The update fixed an intermittent loss of audio during outgoing calls.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition that could occasionally cause audio to drop while placing an outgoing call.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: CFNetwork request-header privacy
changes.canonicalSummary: CFNetwork stopped sending unintended request headers when handling malformed URLs.
changes.summary: Apple repaired malformed-URL handling that could cause unexpected headers to be sent to a server and disclose sensitive information.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: HFS disk-image validation
changes.canonicalSummary: HFS catalog parsing was hardened against an integer underflow in crafted disk images.
changes.summary: The update corrected an underflow that Apple said could cause shutdown or arbitrary code execution when a malicious disk image was mounted.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Kernel sandbox enforcement
changes.canonicalSummary: The kernel corrected debug-system-call handling that could bypass application sandbox restrictions.
changes.summary: Apple fixed a logic error that could let a malicious program execute code in another program with the same user privileges.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: DNS resource-record parsing
changes.canonicalSummary: libresolv corrected an integer overflow in DNS resource-record handling.
changes.summary: The parser was hardened against crafted DNS data that could terminate an application or corrupt heap memory and enable code execution.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Passcode Lock gesture handling
changes.canonicalSummary: The lock screen corrected a race condition involving slide-to-dial gestures.
changes.summary: Apple addressed a physical-access sequence that could bypass Passcode Lock through competing slide-to-dial actions.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Safari Private Browsing history
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari stopped recording certain script-driven visits while Private Browsing was active.
changes.summary: Visits produced through the pushState or replaceState JavaScript methods were prevented from appearing in browser history during a private session.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Siri lock-screen Mail restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: Siri no longer forwarded the active Mail message while invoked from a locked device.
changes.summary: The lock-screen policy was tightened so a voice command could not send a frontmost email message to an arbitrary recipient without unlocking.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: VPN configuration-file validation
changes.canonicalSummary: VPN configuration parsing was hardened against a format-string vulnerability.
changes.summary: Apple repaired racoon configuration-file handling that could allow crafted system configuration data to run code with system privileges.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: WebKit origin and memory safety
changes.canonicalSummary: WebKit corrected cookie disclosure, cross-origin scripting, drag-and-drop, and memory-corruption defects.
changes.summary: The advisory groups fixes for cross-origin isolation and a broad set of memory-safety flaws, including cases capable of script injection, data disclosure, or arbitrary code execution.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

events.summary: The public iOS 5.1.1 update focused on HDR, cellular, AirPlay, Safari synchronization, and purchase-alert reliability plus Safari and WebKit security fixes.

changes.title: Lock-screen HDR reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: HDR capture became more reliable when Camera was opened from the lock-screen shortcut.
changes.summary: Apple improved use of the HDR option specifically for photos taken after entering Camera through the lock screen.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5.1.1 — HDR and Lock Screen shortcut

changes.title: Third-generation iPad cellular switching
changes.canonicalSummary: The update fixed defects that could prevent the third-generation iPad from changing between 2G and 3G service.
changes.summary: Apple addressed cellular-mode switching failures on the device it described at the time as the new iPad.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: AirPlay video playback
changes.canonicalSummary: The update corrected defects affecting AirPlay video playback in some conditions.
changes.summary: Apple records an AirPlay video reliability repair without identifying the affected content type or receiving hardware.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Safari bookmarks and Reading List sync
changes.canonicalSummary: Synchronization reliability improved for Safari bookmarks and Reading List.
changes.summary: The update addressed reliability of keeping bookmark and Reading List data synchronized.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

citations.locator: iOS 5.1.1 — Safari bookmarks and Reading List

changes.title: Post-purchase alert accuracy
changes.canonicalSummary: A misleading unable-to-purchase alert was removed from successful purchase flows.
changes.summary: Apple fixed a condition in which the system could report that a purchase failed even though it had completed successfully.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: Safari location-bar integrity
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari improved URL handling to prevent a crafted site from spoofing the address shown in the location bar.
changes.summary: The browser corrected an address-display weakness that could make a malicious page appear to belong to a legitimate domain.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: WebKit cross-site scripting protection
changes.canonicalSummary: WebKit corrected multiple cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.
changes.summary: Apple addressed two documented WebKit conditions in which malicious web content could cross site boundaries and execute script.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.

changes.title: WebKit memory safety
changes.canonicalSummary: WebKit corrected a memory-corruption flaw reachable through malicious web content.
changes.summary: The browser engine fixed a memory-safety issue Apple said could terminate an application or allow arbitrary code execution.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched to Apple’s version-specific consumer notes, security advisory, announcement, or developer documentation for this release.
